question: What is a major duty of a psychiatric nurse working in a half-way house?

options.A: Monitoring medication adherence and watching for relapse signs
options.B: Performing complex neurosurgeries in the facility parlor
options.C: Cooking all meals for the residents every single day
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of the entire housing estate

question: You want to run a mental health awareness campaign in a rural Nigerian village. Who should you partner with first?

options.A: International aviation safety inspectors
options.B: Private corporate banking executives
options.C: Local village heads and religious leaders
options.D: Foreign pharmaceutical researchers

explanation: Community gatekeepers like elders and religious leaders are trusted by the people. Working with them first opens the door for your message to be accepted!

question: What does 'Unity of Command' mean for teams working in an emergency center?

options.A: All medical decisions must be made by a committee vote before taking action
options.B: Every agency operates independently without communicating with others
options.C: Every worker reports to a designated supervisor to prevent conflicting directions
options.D: The nursing staff holds absolute authority over all logistical operations

explanation: Unity of command keeps things simple: everyone answers to one clear boss so nobody gets mixed up by conflicting orders.

question: Why don't we usually place supercomputers at a patient's bedside in a general ward?

options.A: They are too fragile to be touched by clinical nursing staff
options.B: They cannot process digital data formats used in nursing notes
options.C: Their immense processing power is unnecessary and impractical for daily clinical charting
options.D: They lack the ability to connect to modern electrical wall sockets

explanation: Exactly. Using a supercomputer for normal bedside charting is like using a cargo plane to drive to the local market—complete overkill!

question: The influence of community elders and traditional birth attendants on health choices is an example of which type of determinant?

options.A: Genetic
options.B: Socio-cultural
options.C: Pharmacological
options.D: Molecular

explanation: Spot on! Cultural norms, traditions, and the advice of respected community elders are classic socio-cultural determinants that shape how people view health.

question: Why do red blood cells take on a crescent or sickle shape in sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Dehydration causes the bone marrow to manufacture flat instead of round cells
options.B: Excess iron in the bloodstream physically crushes the cells into sharp points
options.C: White blood cells attack the red blood cells and reshape their outer membranes
options.D: Abnormal haemoglobin molecules stick together to form rigid rods when oxygen is low

explanation: Think of it like a chain reaction: when oxygen drops, HbS molecules clump into stiff rods that push the cell into that classic crescent sickle shape.

question: What do you call a menu that repeats itself after a set time, like every two weeks?

options.A: Static menu
options.B: Single-use menu
options.C: A la carte menu
options.D: Cycle menu

explanation: A cycle menu rotates through a set list of days, which is a lifesaver for busy hospitals and schools.

question: Why do cystine stones form much faster when the urine is acidic?

options.A: Acidic conditions accelerate the speed of the glomerular filtration rate
options.B: Low pH causes the kidneys to manufacture more amino acids
options.C: Cystine has very poor solubility at a low pH level
options.D: Acidic urine destroys the protective lining of the renal pelvis

explanation: Cystine doesn't like to dissolve in acid! When urine is acidic, cystine clumps together instead of staying dissolved, turning into stubborn little crystals and stones.

question: How do cross-sectional study findings help Nigerian nurse managers in clinical practice?

options.A: By proving which nurse caused specific patient readmissions
options.B: By eliminating the need for daily nursing shift handovers
options.C: By guaranteeing permanent funding from international donor agencies
options.D: By providing local data to improve resource allocation and healthcare planning

explanation: Local data helps managers see real community needs clearly, making it easier to send staff and supplies right where they are needed most.

question: Why is it important to write down how the patient tolerated the treatment and how much mucus they cleared?

options.A: It shows how much water the machine used up
options.B: It proves the effectiveness of the treatment
options.C: It determines the hospital room billing costs
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical assessment

explanation: Brilliant! Documenting their response helps the whole healthcare team see that the therapy was successful.

question: What is the ultimate goal for many participants in a sheltered workshop?

options.A: Remaining in the workshop facility for their entire lives
options.B: Starting an independent manufacturing business alone
options.C: Becoming full-time nursing instructors in hospitals
options.D: Transitioning into open, competitive employment

explanation: These workshops are meant to be a helpful stepping stone toward regular, independent jobs in the community. Almost done with this set!

question: A Nigerian ward experiences frequent equipment mix-ups during emergencies. Which simple, low-cost fix would help the most?

options.A: Requiring nurses to memorize every device manual word-for-word
options.B: Color-coding emergency trolley drawers and standardizing equipment placement
options.C: Stopping all patient admissions until brand new imported machines arrive
options.D: Firing all junior nurses to reduce crowding around the storage area

explanation: Simple visual aids like color-coding and tidy, consistent layouts save precious seconds during emergencies without needing expensive high-tech gear!

question: How long is the rectal segment of the large intestine approximately?

options.A: 50 to 60 centimeters
options.B: 12 to 15 centimeters
options.C: 1 to 2 centimeters
options.D: 1 to 2 meters

explanation: The human rectum is roughly 12 to 15 cm long before ending at the anal canal. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is the medical name for those soft spots you feel on a baby's head?

options.A: Fontanelles
options.B: Sutures
options.C: Cranial plates
options.D: Molding joints

explanation: Great job! Fontanelles are simply the membrane-covered spaces where the bones of an infant's skull meet.

question: Who are considered key stakeholders in community mobilisation?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.B: Pharmaceutical company owners only
options.C: Patients admitted to distant urban hospitals
options.D: Only foreign aid workers from abroad

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are influential figures who help guide community opinions and behaviours. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: What does 'pre-testing' mean when creating IEC materials?

options.A: Testing patients' blood pressure before handing out health flyers
options.B: Evaluating nurses on their ability to give health talks
options.C: Showing draft materials to a small sample of the target audience before mass production
options.D: Checking the chemical quality of the paper and ink in a laboratory

explanation: Pre-testing is like a trial run. It lets you spot confusing parts or cultural mistakes before you waste money printing thousands of copies.

question: Why must nurses strictly follow the doctor's weight-bearing orders during mobility training?

options.A: To prevent the client from building too much muscle too quickly
options.B: To protect healing bones and surgical repairs from excessive stress
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing mobility equipment
options.D: To ensure the client does not burn an excessive number of calories

explanation: Spot on! Putting too much weight on a healing bone or fresh surgery too soon can mess up the repair and cause setbacks.

question: What is the largest component of total daily energy expenditure for most people?

options.A: Planned athletic exercise
options.B: Basal or resting metabolic rate
options.C: Adaptive thermogenesis
options.D: Thermic effect of food

explanation: Keeping your internal organs alive and functioning at rest takes up the vast majority of the calories you burn daily. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h3)

question: What is the main financial goal of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) programs?

options.A: Providing multi-million-dollar corporate loans
options.B: Empowering individuals through local skill acquisition and vocational training
options.C: Ending the need for all medical care
options.D: Taking over family legal responsibilities

explanation: CBR helps people learn practical trades using local resources so they can stand on their own feet financially.

question: What does the "principle of adequacy" mean when planning your learning tasks?

options.A: Changing the clinical ward placement every single week
options.B: Providing enough time and practice for you to master the skill
options.C: Ensuring the activity matches the current economic status of the school
options.D: Selecting tasks that only require reading textbooks in the library

explanation: Adequacy is all about giving you enough time and tries to truly master a skill before moving on. Practice makes progress!

question: What is the main reason hospitals conduct pre-employment health checks for new nursing staff?

options.A: To establish a baseline health status and ensure fitness for the job
options.B: To lower the hospital's monthly utility and supply expenses
options.C: To test the worker's knowledge of medical terminology
options.D: To guarantee that the worker will never contract a disease at work

explanation: Checking your health before you start helps the hospital know you're fit for the ward's demands and gives a clear record of your health baseline.

question: In patient safety, what is a "near miss"?

options.A: A patient who successfully recovers from a major illness
options.B: An error that almost happened or was caught just before harming the patient
options.C: A medication that was prescribed but never manufactured
options.D: A nurse who arrived just seconds before her shift started

explanation: Wonderful! A near miss is a free warning sign that lets us fix problems before a real patient is hurt.

question: Which method is best when teaching a community with low literacy levels?

options.A: Giving long lectures without any visual props or pictures
options.B: Using visual aids, drama, and group demonstrations
options.C: Writing detailed medical prescriptions on the chalkboard
options.D: Distributing dense scientific textbooks to every household

explanation: Correct! Pictures, role-play, and practical demos bypass reading barriers and make health messages fun and easy to grasp.

question: What is the main goal of giving Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT)?

options.A: To stop the bowels from moving immediately
options.B: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes using the gut
options.C: To kill the bacteria causing the stomach infection
options.D: To provide full daily nutritional calories

explanation: Spot on! ORT uses the body's natural drinking process to safely put back all the water and essential mineral salts that were washed away.

question: Why is ensuring a deep latch crucial during early breastfeeding sessions?

options.A: It prevents maternal nipple pain and ensures milk transfer
options.B: It triggers immediate passage of meconium stools
options.C: It stops the baby from swallowing excess air bubbles
options.D: It keeps the baby's body temperature stable

explanation: A deep latch puts the milk ducts in the baby's mouth rather than just the nipple, protecting the mother from damage while getting milk out effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h6)

question: What tragic emotional outcome is sometimes seen among young brides who feel completely trapped with no way out?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Suicide and self-harm
options.C: Dissociative identity disorder
options.D: Pathological compulsive gambling

explanation: That's correct. Overwhelming hopelessness and a lack of support drive some desperate young brides to self-harm or suicide.

question: What is the main reason for routine health checkups before hiring food handlers?

options.A: To detect communicable diseases before workers start preparing food
options.B: To assess how well workers can handle high-stress kitchen environments
options.C: To determine the correct salary grade for each new kitchen employee
options.D: To test the physical strength and endurance of kitchen staff

explanation: Screenings catch infectious illnesses early so sick or asymptomatic workers don't spread germs to customers. Brilliant!

question: Which of the following is a core objective of government food intervention?

options.A: Ensuring food security for all citizens
options.B: Eliminating all small-scale family farming
options.C: Maximizing profits for fast-food corporations
options.D: Guaranteeing free food for international export

explanation: Food security is a primary objective, ensuring that everyone has access to safe and nutritious food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: What does the presence of *Escherichia coli* in a well water sample indicate?

options.A: Recent fecal contamination from warm-blooded animals
options.B: High concentration of dissolved iron minerals
options.C: Natural mineral runoff from nearby rocks
options.D: Exposed electrical wiring inside the pump

explanation: E. coli lives primarily in animal and human guts, so finding it in water proves that waste matter has entered the source. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) primarily aim to discover?

options.A: How much financial compensation the patient should receive
options.B: The underlying system flaws that allowed the incident to happen
options.C: Which specific nurse made the final active mistake
options.D: Whether the doctor wrote the medication order correctly

explanation: Brilliant! RCA goes beyond surface blame to find the deep-seated organizational causes of an error. Keep up the awesome daily habit!

question: What is the big giveaway that a study is non-experimental?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate any variables
options.B: Participants are randomly assigned to a treatment
options.C: A new drug is tested on a control group
options.D: Data is collected exclusively through interviews

explanation: Correct! In non-experimental studies, you just observe what is happening naturally without changing or meddling with anything.

question: Why do patriarchal community norms negatively affect child health outcomes?

options.A: They restrict mothers from making independent medical choices for sick children
options.B: They encourage mothers to lead community health committees
options.C: They force fathers to spend all their income on infant vaccines
options.D: They automatically increase the nutritional value of local foods

explanation: When mothers lack household authority, they cannot easily take a sick child to the clinic without prior approval from male heads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h4)

question: What is the main goal of supported housing for patients on psychiatric parole?

options.A: To punish individuals who fail to follow hospital rules
options.B: To provide a safe middle ground between total hospitalization and living alone
options.C: To serve as a permanent replacement for outpatient clinics
options.D: To keep patients completely isolated from the outside community

explanation: Spot on! Supported housing gives patients the right amount of supervision and structure while letting them practice real-world living.

question: How do farmers' markets help build trust between buyers and their food?

options.A: By ensuring that all food items are processed in distant factories
options.B: By hiding the origin of the produce to protect trade secrets
options.C: By shipping all unsold food to foreign countries
options.D: By allowing buyers to ask growers directly about farming methods

explanation: Correct! Chatting face-to-face with the person who grew your food creates amazing transparency and peace of mind.

question: Why does an RCA team repeatedly ask 'why' an incident occurred?

options.A: To delay reporting the incident to hospital executives for as long as possible
options.B: To prove that the patient contributed to their own injury
options.C: To interrogate nurses until they admit fault for their careless actions
options.D: To trace the chain of events back to the fundamental systemic breakdown

explanation: Asking 'why' multiple times peels back superficial layers of error to expose the real root cause in the workflow or environment. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why do we need to eat water-soluble vitamins more often than fat-soluble ones?

options.A: They are destroyed immediately by stomach acid during digestion.
options.B: They turn into toxic waste products if they stay in the bloodstream.
options.C: They are burned up instantly for energy during physical exercise.
options.D: They wash out easily and cannot be stored in large amounts in the body.

explanation: Water-soluble vitamins dissolve in body fluids, and whatever your body doesn't use is passed out in your urine. That's why you need a fresh supply regularly!

question: What is the very first thing a healthcare team must do after a serious adverse event?

options.A: Filing a formal police report against the hospital
options.B: Immediate stabilization and care of the patient
options.C: Notifying the international health organization
options.D: Calling a press conference to explain the mistake

explanation: The patient's safety and clinical stabilization always come first right after any unexpected event happens.

question: Which organs are prioritized and receive redirected blood flow during early shock?

options.A: The kidneys and the stomach
options.B: The skin and the skeletal muscles
options.C: The liver and the intestines
options.D: The brain and the heart

explanation: The body's survival reflex constricts vessels in less vital areas like the skin and gut to ensure the brain and heart continue to receive oxygen. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h2)

question: What is the main reason we use computers and digital tools in clinical nursing?

options.A: To make healthcare delivery safer and more efficient
options.B: To reduce the number of registered nurses needed in a hospital
options.C: To eliminate all verbal communication among healthcare team members
options.D: To completely replace the need for physical bedside nursing assessments

explanation: You got it! Technology is there to back you up as a nurse—reducing mistakes and saving time—not to take away your vital human touch.

question: Why do researchers run a pilot test before the main study starts?

options.A: To identify confusing questions and logistical flaws on a small scale
options.B: To force hospital administrators to approve the study immediately
options.C: To publish the final research paper ahead of all other researchers
options.D: To replace the need for formal ethical clearance from the review board

explanation: A pilot test is like a dress rehearsal. It helps you catch messy questions or flaws before you roll out the full study.

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing sheltered workshops in Nigeria?

options.A: Societal stigma against individuals with mental illness
options.B: Excessive government funding and massive financial surpluses
options.C: Geographical concentration mainly in large urban centers
options.D: Erratic power supply and a lack of raw materials

explanation: Sheltered workshops in Nigeria actually struggle with severe underfunding and lack of resources, not too much money! Keep going!

question: In SOAP charting, what kind of details go into the 'O' (Objective) section?

options.A: The patient's personal feelings and complaints
options.B: The nurse's personal opinion about the diagnosis
options.C: Measurable data like vital signs and lab results
options.D: The future medical orders written by the doctor

explanation: Correct! Objective data means facts you can measure, see, or test, like blood pressure and lab values.

question: When first rinsing used surgical instruments, why should you use cool water instead of hot water?

options.A: Hot water causes proteins to bake onto the metal surface
options.B: Cool water makes the instruments easier to grip with gloves
options.C: Cool water is cheaper for hospital utility budgets
options.D: Hot water damages the outer coating of stainless steel

question: Where does a QA committee usually gather its data to check hospital performance?

options.A: Personal diary entries written by hospital visitors
options.B: Weather forecasts and local market price lists
options.C: Social media gossip and daily newspaper headlines
options.D: Patient feedback forms, pharmacy logs, and health records

explanation: Correct! Reliable data comes straight from official hospital records and direct feedback from our patients.

question: What key engineering feature protects underground water sources underneath a proper sanitary landfill?

options.A: Open drainage ditches filled with gravel
options.B: Deep burning pits without concrete walls
options.C: Direct connection to municipal storm water pipes
options.D: Impermeable bottom liners and leachate collection systems

explanation: Special heavy-duty bottom liners and drainage pipes catch contaminated liquids (leachate) so they don't soak down into our drinking water table.

question: About how long does it usually take for antidepressant medications to start showing noticeable improvements?

options.A: Two to four weeks
options.B: A few minutes
options.C: Twenty-four hours
options.D: Six months

explanation: Correct! Antidepressants take time to build up in the body. Patients usually need to wait two to four weeks before feeling the real benefits.

question: Where should you look in a published study to find the actual numbers and statistical findings?

options.A: The Results section
options.B: The Acknowledgments page
options.C: The Introduction section
options.D: The Table of Contents

explanation: The Results section is where researchers lay out the raw numbers and facts of what they found, without any extra fluff.

question: Why should nursing educators pay attention to environmental factors?

options.A: It helps them design learning spaces that reduce barriers and support success
options.B: It removes the need to give difficult assignments to nursing students
options.C: It guarantees that every student will pass their board exams on the first try
options.D: It allows them to grade clinical paperwork much faster

explanation: When lecturers recognize outside influences, they can adjust the learning space to help you overcome hurdles and thrive. Great job thinking like a future nurse educator!

question: A 16-year-old patient is hesitant to talk about drug use while their mother sits right by the bed. What should you do?

options.A: Document that the patient is uncooperative and end the assessment
options.B: Force the patient to answer the questions in front of the parent
options.C: Threaten to call the police if the patient does not speak up
options.D: Ask the mother to step out briefly to ensure confidential communication

explanation: Spot on! Teens need a safe, confidential space to open up about sensitive topics without worrying about getting into trouble with their parents.

question: What mainly determines whether a person with cerebral palsy will live independently as an adult?

options.A: The severity of the physical impairment and presence of associated cognitive or communication deficits
options.B: The specific month of the year that the original brain injury took place
options.C: The total number of siblings living in the same household
options.D: Whether the infant received physical therapy before turning six months old

explanation: How much independence a person achieves depends mostly on how severely their movement, thinking, and communication are affected by the injury.

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect your pupils?

options.A: It causes dilation to let in more light
options.B: It causes involuntary blinking movements
options.C: It causes constriction to protect the retina
options.D: It has no direct effect on pupil size

explanation: When danger strikes, your pupils widen (dilate) so you can take in more visual details of your surroundings.

question: How does a cold compress help reduce pain?

options.A: By increasing the local metabolic rate of damaged cells
options.B: By slowing down nerve conduction velocity to numb the site
options.C: By permanently destroying local sensory pain receptors
options.D: By flushing out inflammatory toxins through massive vasodilation

explanation: Cold temperatures slow down how fast nerve signals travel, acting like a natural, gentle local anesthetic for the skin.

question: Why does showing great clinical skills make someone a better leader?

options.A: It allows them to work completely independently of doctors.
options.B: It prevents patients from ever filing formal complaints.
options.C: It exempts them from doing any paperwork during their shifts.
options.D: It sets a benchmark that encourages staff to strive for excellence.

explanation: Actions speak louder than words! When your team sees you performing nursing procedures with skill and care, they feel inspired to bring their A-game too.

question: A healthy toddler suddenly starts eating less food than before. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Growth velocity naturally slows down after infancy, reducing food demand
options.B: The child is entering a severe phase of permanent nutritional failure
options.C: Breast milk or formula is no longer needed in any form
options.D: The child has developed an irreversible eating disorder

explanation: Don't panic if a toddler's appetite dips! Because growth slows down after year one, they simply don't need as many calories per kilogram. It's completely normal.

question: Why do we need interprofessional teamwork for a successful quality improvement project?

options.A: Accreditation bodies force everyone to join committees
options.B: It means we don't have to collect patient data
options.C: Healthcare involves many different departments and professional roles
options.D: Doctors refuse to let nurses change routines alone

explanation: You got it! Patient care involves doctors, pharmacists, cleaners, and nurses. Everyone brings a vital piece of the puzzle, so teamwork is a must.

question: At what angle should you insert the needle for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 10 to 15 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 60 degrees
options.D: 45 degrees

explanation: Awesome! A shallow 10 to 15-degree angle is the secret to keeping that needle tip resting nicely right inside the thin dermal layer.

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do you actually carry out your new idea on a small scale?

options.A: Do phase
options.B: Act phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Plan phase

explanation: The 'Do' phase is where the action happens! You test your idea on the ward and see how it works in real life.

question: Why shouldn't you rely purely on assumptions when planning a new community health program?

options.A: Assumptions automatically increase the spread of infectious diseases
options.B: Assumptions are illegal to use in official government health reports
options.C: Assumptions take more time to calculate than actual field surveys
options.D: Assumptions often lead to programs addressing problems the community does not prioritize

explanation: Exactly! If you plan based on guesses instead of facts, you might end up solving problems the locals don't even care about, leading to wasted effort.

question: What is the big difference between bactericidal and bacteriostatic drugs?

options.A: Bactericidal agents require acidic pH, while bacteriostatic agents need alkaline pH
options.B: Bacteriostatic drugs work only in the lungs, while bactericidal drugs work everywhere
options.C: Bactericidal drugs kill bacteria, whereas bacteriostatic drugs stop their growth
options.D: Bacteriostatic drugs destroy human cells, but bactericidal drugs protect them

explanation: Easy to remember: Bacterici-DAL drugs outright KILL the bacteria, while bacteriostatic drugs just press 'pause' on their growth and let your immune system finish the job!

question: How does simply washing your hands actually get rid of tiny germs?

options.A: Through chemical destruction of bacterial cell walls
options.B: By lowering the skin temperature to freeze microbes
options.C: By sealing the pores so bacteria cannot escape
options.D: Through mechanical friction and rinsing under running water

explanation: Think of rubbing your hands together like a broom—the friction scrubs dirt and germs loose, and the running water washes them right down the drain!

question: Why is building a trusting relationship especially important during home health visits?

options.A: It guarantees that the infant will sleep through the night.
options.B: It stops family members from asking questions about the treatment.
options.C: It encourages the mother to share open and honest details about her health.
options.D: It legally protects the nursing agency from any liability issues.

explanation: Trust helps patients feel safe, making them more likely to share true symptoms and personal concerns that affect their care. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which airway opening technique should you use if you suspect a neck injury in a cardiac arrest patient?

options.A: Lateral recovery position
options.B: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.C: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver
options.D: Neck-hyperextension technique

explanation: Safety first! The jaw-thrust lets you open the airway without bending or moving the neck, keeping the cervical spine safe in trauma cases.

question: What does interdependence mean within a healthcare system?

options.A: Every hospital department operates completely on its own
options.B: A change or delay in one part directly affects other parts
options.C: Financial profit is shared equally among all workers
options.D: Only doctors have an impact on overall patient recovery

explanation: Interdependence means elements rely on each other, so a failure or slowdown in one area ripples through the rest of the system. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of these describes a normal (eutocic) labour?

options.A: Surgical induction with a breech presentation at 35 weeks
options.B: Prolonged stages requiring vacuum extraction
options.C: Preterm delivery with multiple interventions
options.D: Spontaneous onset with a cephalic presentation at term

question: During a home assessment, which physical sign points strongly to long-term protein lack?

options.A: Flushed red cheeks
options.B: Yellowing of the sclera
options.C: Temporal wasting
options.D: Excessive hair growth

explanation: When the body lacks protein over time, it starts breaking down its own muscles for fuel. Hollowing around the temples (temporal wasting) is a classic telltale sign.

question: Why must nurses avoid typing patient-identifying details into public or unsecured search tools?

options.A: Search engines are unable to process medical words
options.B: The computer will instantly delete all nursing research files
options.C: Public search engines will charge the hospital a heavy fine
options.D: It violates patient data privacy and confidentiality ethics

explanation: Protecting patient identity is a core nursing duty, and entering identifiable health data into unsecured tools risks privacy breaches. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h8)

question: Why is family planning considered a key pillar of safe motherhood?

options.A: It helps women space pregnancies to protect their physical health
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.C: It completely stops women from experiencing menopause
options.D: It guarantees that every baby born will be a male child

explanation: Giving mum's body time to rest and rebuild strength between babies means a healthier mother and a safer next pregnancy!

question: What is the main reason we use a t-test in nursing research?

options.A: To measure the blood pressure of patients
options.B: To compare the averages of two groups
options.C: To calculate the total sample size needed
options.D: To observe patient behavior in a clinic

explanation: Think of a t-test as a simple way to check if the average score of one group is genuinely different from another group. You've got this!

question: What is the main class of drugs used to treat parasitic worm infections?

options.A: Anthelmintics
options.B: Antivirals
options.C: Antifungals
options.D: Antiseptics

question: What usually happens right away to a community when its food supply chain breaks down?

options.A: Lower rates of chronic illness among residents
options.B: The permanent closure of all local hospitals
options.C: An immediate surplus of fresh vegetables in every market
options.D: Food scarcity and sudden price inflation

explanation: When transport and supply routes fail, food becomes hard to find, and whatever is left usually shoots up in price.

question: Why is the immune system called a 'diffuse' system instead of just one single organ?

options.A: It relies entirely on the brain to direct every defensive action
options.B: It only functions when a person is actively sleeping or resting
options.C: It changes its physical structure completely every few days
options.D: It consists of cells, tissues, and organs spread throughout the body

explanation: Unlike the heart which stays in one place, your immune cells are everywhere! They travel through your blood, lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow all at once.

question: What technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

options.A: Dry microwave pulses
options.B: Deep freezing cold
options.C: High-pressure steam
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation

explanation: Autoclaves use high-pressure steam and intense heat to wipe out harmful microorganisms effectively. You'll see these in action often!

question: Which behavioral change is a classic warning sign of potential substance abuse?

options.A: Neglecting work or school responsibilities
options.B: Consistent weight gain and healthy skin tone
options.C: An increased interest in family activities
options.D: Sudden improvement in daily sleep routines

explanation: Correct! When substances take center stage in someone's life, important commitments like classes, work, and family duties usually start slipping away.

question: After a safe delivery, which eye ointment do you apply right away to protect a newborn from eye infections?

options.A: Atropine sulfate drops
options.B: Chloramphenicol eye drops
options.C: Hydrocortisone eye gel
options.D: Tetracycline eye ointment

explanation: Brilliant! Tetracycline 1% eye ointment is standard care to shield baby's eyes from harmful bacteria passed during birth.

question: Which nursing action is most important for getting an accurate weight on a clinical scale?

options.A: Subtracting a standard clothing allowance from whatever scale value appears
options.B: Weighing the patient immediately after they have consumed a large meal
options.C: Ensuring the scale is calibrated and having the patient remove shoes and heavy coats
options.D: Using a spring-loaded bathroom scale brought from home for consistency

explanation: You got it! Checking that the scale is zeroed/calibrated and having the patient shed heavy outer garments ensures you are measuring the patient, not their jacket.

question: How can bedside nurses help lower overall health care costs?

options.A: By preventing hospital-acquired complications and minimizing supply waste
options.B: By charging patients directly for bedside nursing procedures
options.C: By eliminating all diagnostic tests from patient care plans
options.D: By shortening physician consultation times during emergencies

explanation: Stopping problems like pressure sores or infections keeps patients safe, out of intensive care, and saves money on wasted supplies.

question: Why is it an urgent concern if a child's weight line crosses downward across Z-score lines?

options.A: It indicates normal seasonal weight loss in toddlers
options.B: It means the mother has stopped bringing the child to the clinic
options.C: It shows an active deterioration in nutritional status
options.D: It proves the weighing scale was broken during the visit

explanation: Crossing downward means the child is actively losing ground toward malnutrition and needs quick clinical attention.

question: What is a common emotional response experienced by a person who has recently acquired a permanent physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference toward their physical health status
options.B: Immediate and permanent acceptance of the new lifestyle
options.C: Euphoria over lifestyle changes and reduced responsibilities
options.D: Grief and a process similar to mourning a loss

explanation: Patients frequently experience a grief reaction as they process the loss of their previous physical abilities and independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is a big legal no-no when writing nursing notes?

options.A: Using approved hospital acronyms and terminology
options.B: Including judgmental personal opinions about the patient
options.C: Recording objective physical assessment findings
options.D: Documenting factual vital signs immediately after taking them

explanation: Keep notes strictly professional and factual! Writing personal opinions in a chart can cause legal trouble and hurt your credibility.

question: What actually happens during DOTS (Directly Observed Therapy) for a TB patient?

options.A: A health worker watches the patient swallow every dose
options.B: Blood tests are run daily to measure drug levels in the serum
options.C: The patient reports their pill intake via phone once a week
options.D: Family members check the pill bottles at the end of each month

explanation: Under DOTS, a healthcare worker physically watches the patient take their meds to ensure they finish the whole course without missing days.

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) ranked as the least effective way to control hazards?

options.A: It depends on human behavior and can easily fail or be worn incorrectly
options.B: It is always too expensive for companies to purchase in bulk
options.C: It completely removes the hazard from the physical environment
options.D: It increases the physical speed at which employees perform tasks

explanation: PPE is super important, but it's a last line of defense because if a worker forgets to wear it or wears it wrongly, they are still exposed to danger!

question: According to WHO guidelines, which condition is a strict medical reason (Category 4) NOT to use a progestin-only implant?

options.A: Controlled gestational diabetes
options.B: History of heavy menstrual periods
options.C: Mild uncomplicated hypertension
options.D: Current breast cancer

explanation: Active breast cancer is sensitive to hormones, making progestin implants unsafe (Category 4). Patient safety always comes first!

question: What is the main job of a Nurse Principal Investigator?

options.A: Distributing meal trays to study participants in the clinic
options.B: Cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments after research surgeries
options.C: Designing studies, securing funding, and overseeing ethical implementation
options.D: Administering daily bed baths to patients on the surgical ward

explanation: Think of a Principal Investigator as the captain of the study—they plan the project, find financial support, and make sure everything follows ethical guidelines. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: What term describes the emigration of trained health workers to other countries for better pay?

options.A: Epidemiologic transition
options.B: Resource allocation
options.C: Health tourism
options.D: Brain drain

explanation: Brain drain occurs when a country loses its skilled professionals, such as nurses and doctors, who leave for better working conditions and salaries abroad. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is a common local complication of improper injection administration?

options.A: Rapid lowering of blood pressure in healthy individuals
options.B: Pain, tissue necrosis, or abscess formation at the site
options.C: Immediate recovery from chronic respiratory illnesses
options.D: Permanent immunity against all forms of bacterial infection

explanation: Poor injection technique or contaminated medication can cause localized tissue damage, pain, and painful abscesses. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: Why are joint multi-agency simulation drills important before a disaster happens?

options.A: They allow international donors to inspect local hospital buildings
options.B: They build personal trust and working familiarity among different responders
options.C: They eliminate the need for any written emergency response plans
options.D: They guarantee that natural disasters will completely bypass the region

explanation: Training together beforehand ensures that different agencies know each other's styles and work smoothly together when lives are on the line. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h8)

question: A pregnant patient in her second trimester complains of heartburn and mild constipation. What's the most likely culprit?

options.A: Hormone-induced slowing of the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: An infection of the upper digestive lining
options.C: Consuming too much water with her meals
options.D: The physical weight of the placenta pressing on her stomach

explanation: You nailed it. High progesterone levels slow down bowel movements and relax the stomach valve, causing that familiar pregnancy heartburn and constipation.

question: Why must dangerous infections like cholera be reported immediately to health authorities?

options.A: To ensure the hospital receives full financial reimbursement.
options.B: To update international travel visa records automatically.
options.C: To trigger rapid outbreak containment and protect the community.
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on infected populations.

explanation: Spot on! Quick reporting lets public health teams jump into action, find the source, and stop an epidemic before it spreads.

question: What is the best way to write down a patient's chief complaint in their clinical chart?

options.A: Use the patient's own words inside quotation marks
options.B: Translate their description into complex medical jargon
options.C: Leave the exact wording out and just write your diagnosis
options.D: Summarize what you think they meant in your own words

explanation: Correct! Putting their exact words in quotes keeps their story pure without adding your own guesswork.

question: Why is asking for healthcare different from buying regular everyday goods like shoes or food?

options.A: Patients can easily diagnose and prescribe their own meds
options.B: Healthcare services are always completely free from the government
options.C: Sickness usually happens without warning and patients need professional guidance
options.D: The supply of doctors and nurses is totally unlimited everywhere

explanation: Spot on! You can't really plan when you'll fall ill. Because medical needs come suddenly, patients rely heavily on expert advice rather than just shopping around casually.

question: What is the main job of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) in the kidneys?

options.A: Stimulating the excretion of excess water in urine
options.B: Blocking the reabsorption of sodium ions
options.C: Promoting water reabsorption into the blood
options.D: Increasing the production of red blood cells

explanation: Think of ADH as your body's water-saver. When you're running low on fluids, ADH tells your kidneys to hold onto water and put it back into your bloodstream.

question: What are the three core things a basic computer does?

options.A: Storing drug dosages, calculating IV rates, and updating policies
options.B: Printing paper records, scanning IDs, and filing charts
options.C: Accepting data, processing it, and producing information
options.D: Connecting to the internet, sending emails, and blocking viruses

explanation: Think of a computer like a helpful assistant: it takes raw facts in, does some work on them, and gives you useful results for patient care!

question: What is the primary practical purpose of estimating maternal mortality in a country?

options.A: To determine the total population growth rate of newborns
options.B: To punish hospitals that report high numbers of patient deaths
options.C: To allocate healthcare resources and target interventions effectively
options.D: To calculate annual tax deductions for pregnant mothers

explanation: Accurate estimates allow health planners to see where the greatest dangers lie and direct resources and emergency care improvements to those areas. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h2)

question: What does juvenile delinquency mean?

options.A: Severe mental illness manifesting during early adolescent years
options.B: Disobedient behavior shown exclusively within a school environment
options.C: Illegal actions committed by individuals below the age of majority
options.D: Minor disobedience corrected entirely through parental discipline

explanation: You've got this! Juvenile delinquency simply means unlawful actions done by young people who are not yet adults legally. Think of it as youth breaking the law.

question: What is the recommended daily percentage range for total fat intake in healthy adults?
explanation: Aiming for 20% to 35% of daily calories from fats keeps adults energized and healthy without overdoing it. You're doing great!

question: During an acute asthma attack, why does a patient struggle to catch their breath?

options.A: Degeneration of skeletal muscle in the chest wall
options.B: Paralysis of the diaphragm skeletal muscle
options.C: Failure of cardiac muscle to pump blood to the lungs
options.D: Excessive contraction of airway smooth muscle

explanation: In asthma, the smooth muscle wrapped around the tiny airways spasms and squeezes shut, making it hard for air to move in and out. You'll see this often in practice!

question: Why is sensory reception in the skin vital for overall physical safety?

options.A: It produces essential vitamins when exposed to sunlight
options.B: It warns the brain about dangerous pressure, heat, or injury
options.C: It controls how fast the outer layer of skin cells grows
options.D: It regulates the amount of water lost through the pores

explanation: Sensory receptors detect environmental hazards like extreme heat or sharp pressure so the body can react quickly. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h4)

question: If a drug has a high affinity for a receptor but low intrinsic activity, what happens?

options.A: It is rapidly cleared by the kidneys
options.B: It binds tightly but produces little cellular response
options.C: It fails to bind to the receptor at all
options.D: It produces a very strong and immediate reaction

explanation: Affinity is about sticking to the receptor, while intrinsic activity is about turning the action on. So it hugs the receptor tightly, but doesn't do much inside!

question: What is the main difference between "diffusion" and "spread" in healthcare?

options.A: Diffusion only happens in clinics, while spread only happens in wards
options.B: Diffusion is passive and unplanned, while spread is active and deliberate
options.C: Diffusion costs money, while spread is completely free of charge
options.D: Diffusion is done by doctors, while spread is done strictly by nurses

explanation: Think of diffusion like gossip spreading naturally, while spread is an intentional, well-planned effort to share a good practice!

question: Why are nurses considered central to safe waste management in a hospital?

options.A: They purchase all the disposal bags and bins
options.B: They are legally required to transport waste off-site
options.C: They design the incinerators used for burning trash
options.D: They generate and dispose of medical waste daily

explanation: Nurses perform procedures like injections and dressing changes every day, meaning they make the first choices about where waste goes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Which sign is most typical in a patient who has damage to Broca's area?

options.A: Inability to hear or recognize spoken words from others
options.B: Trouble speaking fluent words despite understanding language
options.C: Complete paralysis of all four limbs on the right side
options.D: Total loss of long-term memory about childhood events

explanation: This is expressive aphasia: the patient usually knows what they want to say in their head, but getting the words out is the struggle.

question: When is a nebulizer most commonly chosen over a metered-dose inhaler?

options.A: When the patient needs a device that fits easily in a small shirt pocket
options.B: When treatment must be completed in less than five seconds
options.C: When the patient cannot coordinate deep breathing with a handheld inhaler
options.D: When the healthcare provider wants to avoid using any electricity or gas

explanation: Nebulizers produce a continuous mist over several minutes, making them great for young children, the elderly, or acutely breathless patients. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main danger of leaving a bacterial swab at room temperature for too long before it gets to the lab?

options.A: Fragile bacteria may die and contaminants may overgrow
options.B: The patient's name will fade off the specimen label
options.C: The transport gel will turn into a solid block of ice
options.D: The plastic shaft will melt and ruin the collection tip

explanation: Time is of the essence! If left too long, fast-growing germs take over, masking the real culprit and ruining the test results.

question: Which item is a major source of hidden sodium in many Nigerian home-cooked meals?

options.A: Fresh green vegetables
options.B: Seasoning stock cubes
options.C: Raw unrefined palm oil
options.D: Unprocessed yellow garri

explanation: Seasoning cubes are packed with sodium and are frequently added in multiple quantities to local soups and stews. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using qualitative tools in a community assessment?

options.A: To capture local attitudes, cultural beliefs, and human stories
options.B: To measure precise blood pressure and body temperature
options.C: To calculate exact mathematical disease prevalence rates
options.D: To count the total number of hospital beds in the district

explanation: Brilliant! Qualitative methods help you understand the 'why' behind people's behaviors rather than just raw numbers.

question: Why do families on a tight budget often experience a drop in their diet quality?

options.A: Local markets stop selling fresh vegetables to low-income earners
options.B: Wholesale food vendors refuse to sell small quantities to families
options.C: Nutritional requirements naturally decrease when a person has less money
options.D: They replace nutrient-dense foods with cheap, highly processed options

explanation: Exactly. When funds run low, it's easy to lean towards cheaper, filling items that lack the vital nutrients our bodies really need.

question: What is the primary function of an antibody in the human body?

options.A: To produce energy for cellular reactions
options.B: To carry oxygen to body tissues
options.C: To identify and neutralize foreign antigens
options.D: To clot blood after an injury occurs

explanation: Antibodies are immune proteins designed to bind specifically to foreign invaders and toxins, marking them for destruction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard security measure used to protect electronic patient records?

options.A: Publicly posting patient medical histories on hospital hallway notice boards
options.B: Password protection and secure login credentials for every clinician
options.C: Biometric fingerprint scanners to verify staff identity at the workstation
options.D: Role-based access controls that limit file viewing to authorized staff

explanation: Posting private health information publicly violates core confidentiality principles and patient privacy laws. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of gerontology?

options.A: The administration of emergency care in intensive care units
options.B: The study of aging and older adults from multiple disciplines
options.C: The surgical treatment of age-related bone fractures
options.D: The pharmacological management of childhood infectious diseases

explanation: Gerontology looks broadly at the physical, mental, and social changes that happen as people grow older. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h1)

question: How are resident skin germs different from the transient germs you pick up on the ward?

options.A: Transient flora permanently live inside the deeper layers of skin tissue
options.B: Transient flora cannot be washed off with regular soap and water
options.C: Resident flora live deep in the skin and are harder to remove completely
options.D: Resident flora are always deadly pathogens that cause quick disease

explanation: Resident flora are like permanent residents tucked deep in your skin crevices, while transient flora just sit loosely on top.

question: Why do patients taking lithium need careful guidance about their salt and water intake?

options.A: Salt completely destroys the chemical structure of the lithium pill
options.B: Lithium alters fluid balance and can easily reach toxic levels if hydration shifts
options.C: Water causes lithium to instantly evaporate inside the human stomach
options.D: Patients on lithium lose all sense of taste for salty foods

explanation: Spot on! Lithium handles similarly to sodium in the kidneys, so dehydration or sudden salt changes can dangerously spike drug levels.

question: Which common habit in the ward is a leading cause of accidental needle-prick injuries for nursing staff?

options.A: Recapping used injection needles
options.B: Using needleless intravenous systems
options.C: Emptying full sharps containers safely
options.D: Placing sharps boxes at eye level

explanation: Never try to recap a used needle! Trying to guide that tiny cap back on with two hands is the number one way nurses accidentally jab their own fingers.

question: What is the primary purpose of using IEC support materials during a health talk?

options.A: To reinforce key health messages and make them easy to remember
options.B: To completely replace the need for verbal health education
options.C: To decorate the community health center walls
options.D: To serve as official medical prescriptions for patients

explanation: Support materials provide visual and tactile reminders that help people retain health information long after the meeting ends. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which home modification is most helpful for preventing bathroom falls?

options.A: Placing soft throw rugs on the tile floor
options.B: Installing grab bars and non-slip mats
options.C: Using dim lighting to avoid harsh glares
options.D: Keeping the bathroom door locked at night

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces are extremely slick, making grab bars and non-slip mats essential safety additions. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why do traditional household rules often cause dangerous delays when women need medical care?

options.A: Cultural norms forbid women from speaking to female nurses
options.B: Traditional beliefs state that women never get sick
options.C: Customs require women to work in hospitals instead of visiting them
options.D: Women may need male approval or funds to seek treatment

explanation: When men hold all the financial and decision-making power, women often have to wait for permission or money, which can dangerously delay healthcare. You're mastering this!

question: Why is putting traditional substances like saliva or dung on a newborn's umbilical cord dangerous?

options.A: It permanently stains the baby's skin around the abdomen
options.B: It prevents the infant from absorbing breast milk
options.C: It causes the umbilical cord to fall off too quickly
options.D: It introduces harmful bacteria that can cause severe infections like tetanus

explanation: The cord stump is a direct highway to the baby's bloodstream. Unclean substances easily bring in fatal germs like tetanus or sepsis. Keep it clean and dry! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Why is herd immunity super important for young babies and people with weak immune systems?

options.A: They produce antibodies much faster than healthy adults
options.B: They live in environments with zero exposure to pathogens
options.C: They cannot safely receive certain vaccines themselves
options.D: They require higher doses of medication to build immunity

explanation: Spot on! When most people around them are vaccinated, it builds a protective shield for those who can't take the shots yet.

question: As you gently bend your patient's neck forward, they automatically bend their knees and hips. What sign is this?

options.A: Normal nuchal flexibility
options.B: A positive Brudzinski's sign
options.C: A negative Kernig's sign
options.D: Early signs of a stroke

explanation: That automatic knee-and-hip-bend when the neck goes forward is a classic positive Brudzinski's sign. It's a clear giveaway for irritated meninges!

question: Why is paying out-of-pocket for medical care at the hospital dangerous for families?

options.A: It increases the cost of medical equipment
options.B: It prevents nurses from administering medications
options.C: It forces families into sudden poverty during health emergencies
options.D: It causes hospitals to close down immediately

explanation: You've got this! Paying directly for care on the spot can wipe out family savings and delay the care someone desperately needs. That's why health financing matters so much.

question: Why is gastrulation such a huge milestone in early human development?

options.A: It marks the exact moment the heart starts its very first visible beat
options.B: It immediately connects the baby's blood supply to the maternal heart
options.C: It causes the embryo to double in size within a single day
options.D: It establishes the three distinct tissue layers that build all body organs

explanation: Gastrulation is like laying down the foundational blueprint (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm) needed to construct every single organ in the body.

question: What can happen if educators overlook cultural differences in communication?

options.A: They will automatically improve student test scores in pharmacology
options.B: They remove all language barriers from clinical wards
options.C: They ensure all students learn at the exact same speed
options.D: They might misinterpret a student's respectful quietness as laziness

explanation: In some cultures, staying completely quiet around elders or teachers is a sign of deep respect. Instructors need to understand this so they don't misjudge a student.

question: A local market association refuses to allow a recovering psychiatric client to sell goods, claiming the person is dangerous. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Report the entire market union to the police for immediate arrest
options.B: Organize an educational session with market leaders to discuss mental health recovery and bust myths
options.C: Advise the client to move to a different town and never work again
options.D: Agree with the leaders because public safety always requires total isolation

explanation: Engaging community leaders directly with education helps correct false fears and promotes the social inclusion of recovering individuals. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is psychological safety so important for keeping quality high on a hospital ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to document routine vital signs on shifts
options.B: It prevents patients from filing lawsuits against individual healthcare workers
options.C: It encourages staff to report errors and suggest changes without fear of punishment
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will receive increased government funding every year

explanation: When nurses feel safe to speak up without getting into trouble, safety issues get fixed before anyone gets hurt.

question: When food prices shoot up way past family incomes, what do households usually do first?

options.A: Growing all required food supplies inside the home
options.B: Stopping all food purchases until prices return to normal
options.C: Replacing nutrient-dense foods with cheap carbohydrates
options.D: Increasing the daily consumption of fresh meat and fish

explanation: When money is tight, families switch to cheap filling carbs and cut out expensive proteins and fresh produce. It's a tough economic reality.

question: Which neurotransmitter is primarily linked to feelings of reward, motivation, and the hallucinations seen in schizophrenia?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Melatonin
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: GABA

explanation: Dopamine pathways regulate reward and motivation, and overactive dopamine signaling is a major factor in psychotic symptoms like hallucinations. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h3)

question: What main change happens inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) during pneumonia?

options.A: The walls permanently stretch and lose stretchiness.
options.B: Blood flow to the lungs completely stops overnight.
options.C: Fluid, pus, and cellular debris fill up the spaces.
options.D: The breathing tubes stretch out and trap air.

explanation: As the body fights the infection, fluid and white blood cells flood the alveoli. That's why air has such a hard time getting in!

question: What is the main job of pulmonary surfactant inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli)?

options.A: To stimulate the diaphragm to contract during inspiration
options.B: To warm incoming air before it reaches the bronchioles
options.C: To transport oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To lower surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse

explanation: You've got this! Surfactant acts like a special coating that reduces surface tension inside the tiny air sacs, keeping them open and stable so breathing is easy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why does the autonomic nervous system use a two-neuron chain instead of just one?

options.A: To prevent any electrical signals from reaching the heart
options.B: To speed up nerve impulses past voluntary motor speeds
options.C: To allow signal relay and amplification outside the central nervous system
options.D: To connect directly to voluntary skeletal muscle fibers

explanation: Think of it like a relay team! Breaking the pathway into two neurons helps spread and multiply the nerve signal so it can reach multiple places effectively.

question: Why is alarm fatigue a dangerous issue with continuous cardiac monitors?

options.A: The monitor stops working after a certain number of alarms
options.B: Staff may ignore or turn down alarms because of too many false warnings
options.C: The batteries in the monitor run out of power too quickly
options.D: Patients get too tired from hearing the screen beep all day

explanation: Constant ringing from non-urgent alerts can cause nurses to miss a real emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: A parole patient misses two clinic appointments in a row. What should the mental health team do?

options.A: Wait patiently until the patient decides to call the clinic back.
options.B: Check in on the patient quickly to see if they are relapsing.
options.C: Assume the patient is doing wonderfully and needs no contact.
options.D: Discharge the patient from the program for breaking the rules.

explanation: That's right! Missing appointments is an early warning sign that symptoms might be worsening or the patient is slipping away from treatment.

question: Why is evaluation an essential final step in every community health program?

options.A: It ensures that no nurse ever makes a mistake in clinical practice
options.B: It proves that health education is more important than medical treatment
options.C: It is required by law to fine community members who missed the sessions
options.D: It helps nurses learn what worked and how to improve future health campaigns

explanation: Evaluation isn't about judging—it's about learning! It helps you see what went well so your next community project can be even better.

question: What does healthcare 'supply' actually measure?

options.A: The total financial debt accumulated by local community hospitals
options.B: The total number of sick people residing within a specific region
options.C: The exact amount of government funding allocated to public health
options.D: The volume of medical services providers are willing and able to offer

explanation: Correct! Supply is simply all the care, beds, and services that hospitals and nurses are ready to provide at any given time.

question: Why should young adult men learn to do regular testicular self-examinations?

options.A: It helps detect lumps or changes early when treatment is most effective
options.B: It stops the development of benign prostatic hyperplasia later in life
options.C: It guarantees complete protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: It prevents the normal age-related decline in testosterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! Just like breast self-exams for women, checking early helps catch unusual lumps or changes when treatment works best.

question: Why must a nurse carefully watch a patient's urine output after starting an anticholinergic anti-spasmodic?

options.A: The drug is filtered out very rapidly by the kidneys
options.B: It prevents the patient from developing severe diarrhea
options.C: It proves the drug is successfully relaxing the stomach
options.D: The medication can cause urinary retention

explanation: Anticholinergics can make it hard for the bladder to squeeze properly, causing urine to get trapped. Always keep an eye on how well your patient is passing urine!

question: Which document tells a nurse NOT to start CPR on an unresponsive patient?

options.A: A general medical insurance policy
options.B: A valid do-not-resuscitate order
options.C: A verbal request from a distant relative
options.D: A standard hospital admission form

explanation: Always respect patient wishes! A signed and valid Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) order or advance directive legally stops us from initiating CPR.

question: Which factor is most important when deciding if a psychiatric patient is ready for parole?

options.A: Having a high-paying job lined up before leaving
options.B: The willingness to move to a different city
options.C: Completing a college degree during the hospital stay
options.D: Stable symptoms and willingness to take medications

explanation: That's right! Before stepping out, a patient needs to show steady mental health and a proven willingness to stick to their treatment plan.

question: Why do pregnant women often develop physiological anaemia?

options.A: Rapid destruction of red blood cells by the placenta
options.B: Severe dietary protein deficiency in early pregnancy
options.C: The bone marrow completely stops making new blood cells
options.D: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cells

explanation: You've got this! Think of it like adding more water to juice: the red blood cells are still there, but the fluid (plasma) increases so much that it gets diluted. This is completely normal in pregnancy!

question: Which of these is an operational expense (OpEx) rather than a capital investment?

options.A: Purchasing a brand-new MRI scanner for the hospital
options.B: Building a completely new wing for pediatric care
options.C: Acquiring a fleet of new ambulances for emergency services
options.D: Daily cleaning supplies used on the ward

explanation: Cleaning supplies are routine, day-to-day items needed to keep the ward running smoothly, making them operational expenses.

question: Why is early identification and screening vital in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience stress again
options.B: It prevents mild symptoms from progressing into severe disorders
options.C: It replaces the need for physical health examinations
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any prescription medications
